title: Implementing GIS tools for automatic detection of riverbed forms
author: Kryniecka

steps.title: Install QGIS and dependencies
steps.instruction: Install QGIS (version compatible with Python 3.9) on your workstation and ensure the Python environment includes PyQt5, Pandas, NumPy, and GDAL.

steps.title: Download Sandbar Detector plugin
steps.instruction: Clone or download the Sandbar Detector plugin from https://github.com/KK-hydro/Sandbar-detector/ and place the plugin folder in the QGIS plugins directory.

steps.title: Obtain Sentinel‑2 Level 1C imagery
steps.instruction: From the Sat4Envi platform, download Sentinel‑2 Level 1C images covering the study stretch of the Vistula River between kilometres 806 and 809 near the Chełmno water gauge, selecting scenes with minimal cloud cover and low water stage to expose sandbars.

steps.title: Select study area in QGIS
steps.instruction: Load the downloaded Sentinel‑2 Level 1C product into QGIS and define the area of interest (AOI) covering km 806‑809; this AOI should include diverse hydrological conditions and visible riverbed forms (sandbars, islands, ripples).

steps.title: Configure plugin spectral bands
steps.instruction: Within the Sandbar Detector plugin, specify the four required Sentinel‑2 bands: Blue, Green, Near‑Infrared (NIR), and Short‑Wave Infrared 1 (SWIR1).

steps.title: Run automated detection
steps.instruction: Execute the plugin; it will compute the SWM (Spectral Water Index) for each pixel, create a binary water‑mask image, and output a final vector layer representing land and water features.

steps.title: Inspect vector product and attributes
steps.instruction: Open the generated vector layer in QGIS; verify that the attribute table contains fields for type (land or water), area, and perimeter for each polygon.

steps.title: Optional: Compare with manual or traditional SWM method
steps.instruction: If desired, manually digitise selected sandbars using QGIS drawing tools or apply the traditional SWM workflow; then compare polygon areas and perimeters with those from the automated vector to assess accuracy, efficiency, and consistency.
